minutes.headline: Budget Task Force heard assessors say a split tax rate would raise commercial bills sharply for small resident savings; not recommended.
minutes.summary: The assessors presented the residential exemption and a split tax rate using estimated numbers. They concluded neither fits Lunenburg: the town is mostly residential, so the shifts save homeowners little and raise commercial bills a lot. The group also discussed the Community Preservation Act and the stormwater utility, reviewed plans for the special town meeting presentation, and approved seven sets of prior minutes by roll call.

budget_items.what_was_said: The average single-family bill would drop only modestly with a shift, while commercial and industrial bills would rise sharply.
Commercial value is much larger than industrial value; commercial is about 8% of the tax base.

The classification hearing was said to be at the select board on the 19th, with the assessor preparing several shifts for three typical homes and some commercial properties.

At town meeting the group will speak rather than use slides.
Next meetings discussed for the 18th, with a flex meeting after.

what_happened.line: The assessors presented the residential exemption and a split tax rate, and concluded neither suits a town that is mostly residential.
Under the estimated scenarios, a split rate would modestly lower the average single-family bill and sharply raise commercial and industrial bills.
Assessors will send the task force data on the top 10 commercial and industrial properties, and a list of business exemptions was requested.
The split tax rate stays on the agenda as a placeholder, to be mentioned at special town meeting only as considered.
The group would recommend that the parks and municipal building design groups examine Community Preservation Act funding with real numbers.

why_it_matters: A split tax rate would move part of the property tax burden from homes to commercial and industrial owners, and the assessors' estimates show the home savings would be small next to the commercial increases.
Community Preservation Act funding is a property tax surcharge with a state match, so it could become a question for annual town meeting that adds to a tax bill.
